subtitle: France and Spain lead the 2026 World Cup winner market at nearly identical implied probabilities due to their exceptional squad depth and recent major-tournament success, with Spain riding post-Euro 2024 momentum and France benefiting from unmatched rotation options around Kylian Mbappé. England sits just behind on the strength of its attacking talent pool under Thomas Tuchel, while Portugal, Brazil, and Argentina remain tightly bunched on historical pedigree and star quality despite varying recent form. The expanded 48-team format and relatively open groups have kept probabilities clustered among these sides, as no single nation has pulled clear on the eve of the tournament and several contenders enter with comparable injury concerns and preparation schedules.
